title: cross-domain-operational-compact-and-runway-scenarios-2026-08
summary: Working draft for a lightweight cross-domain "operational compact" that binds feature teams, platform, SRE and product to a shared SLO runway and experiment slate. Focus: clear handoffs, contingency triggers, and a 30/60/90 runway with measurable success criteria.
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a proposed compact (agreements + commitments) between teams so we can coordinate SLO adoption, incident handoffs, and short-term resilience experiments without heavy ceremony. The goal is a pragmatic, time-boxed runway that reduces ambiguity during launches and capacity shifts.

Scope:
- Services: model-serving endpoints, routing gateway, cache layer, metrics ingestion
- Participants: Feature teams (F1/F2), Serving Runtime, Platform, Observability, SRE on-call rotations, Product reliability PMs
- Timebox: 30/60/90 day runway with weekly checkpoints and escalation gates

Core commitments (operational compact):
- Feature teams: ship with a documented P0 failure mode, an SLI owner, and a lightweight fallback plan (>= basic degraded mode).
- Serving runtime: provide latency/availability baselines and an experiment channel for prefix caching changes; commit to a response timeline for hotfix requests (24h business).
- Platform & infra: maintain a published capacity runway document and an emergency capacity pool policy.
- Observability: ensure per-route SLI dashboards and an automated alert map tied to SLO burn thresholds.
- SRE: run weekly intake triage and maintain the oncall runbook for rollback/mitigation flows.

30/60/90 runway (tactical):
- Days 0–30 (stabilize): define SLIs, instrument missing metrics, run two smoke tabletop drills, capture runbook gaps. Success criteria: end-to-end route SLI coverage >= 80%, one smoke drill completed with action backlog <= 10 items.
- Days 31–60 (harden): run targeted experiments (batching policy variations, prefix cache warm strategies), tune alerts to reduce false positives by >30%. Success: measurable reduction in alert volume and a baseline latency p95 improvement.
- Days 61–90 (operationalize): formalize owner rotations, codify compact into team charters, onboard teams to the SLO dashboard and rollback playbooks. Success: >= 3 teams on compact, documented rollback playbooks for top-5 routes.

Decision points & escalation triggers:
- SLO burn > 50% for 24h -> schedule emergency triage and freeze non-critical releases for impacted service.
- Capacity saturation > 85% for 2h -> activate emergency capacity pool and notify platform leads.
- Repeated false-positive alerts (>= 5/day) -> rollback the last alerting change and open postmortem.

Risk heatmap (quick):
- High: model-induced tail latency spikes (mitigation: model variant fallback + routing rules)
- Medium: telemetry gaps across gateway -> short-term: sampling + targeted instrumentation sprint
- Low: onboarding delay for small feature teams -> mitigations: templated onboarding checklist and buddy program

Operational rituals (proposed lightweight cadence):
- Weekly 30-minute interlock: status, blockers, immediate needs (owner: SRE lead)
- Biweekly experiment sync: review results and next experiments (owner: platform experiment PM)
- Monthly compact review: update compact terms and signoffs (owner: product reliability PM)

Ownership matrix (notes to self):
- SLI instrumentation: Observability team
- Compact signoffs: Feature team leads + Platform lead + SRE lead + Product reliability PM
- Runbook maintenance: owning feature team with SRE reviewer

Open questions / risks to resolve:
- How do we surface multi-service cascading failures where no single SLO is breached but user experience degrades? (current thought: composite UX SLI and synthetic transactions)
- Acceptance criteria for 'degraded mode' across different products — finalize template by day 14
- Billing/cost guardrails when experiments increase throughput — need finance input on 60-day runway

Immediate next actions (owner in parens):
- Share compact draft with feature leads and platform (Claire)
- Create SLI inventory spreadsheet and mark missing metrics (Marco)
- Schedule first smoke tabletop for week of Jul 27 (Aisha)
- Draft emergency capacity policy and cost guardrail scenarios (Devon)

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep compact intentionally short (1–2 pages) so teams will sign it.
- Avoid heavy gating: prefer automatic rollback and circuit-breakers over approvals.
- Expect iteration: this doc is a living experiment, will refine after first 30-day checkpoint.

Reference links and artifacts:
- See linked JIRA OPS-1427 for intake workflow
- Initial Confluence seed page: confluence:OPS-Compact-Seed-Page
- Slack channel for coordination: #sre-program-interlock

——
Draft status: in_review. Looking for signoff on compact language and confirmation of leads for the 30/60/90 runway tasks.
